cohort: Pregnant mice were administered different dosages of methylmercury chloride (MMC) via gavage to establish models of embryonic malformation.
finding: Noninvasive dual-modality photoacoustic-ultrasound (PA-US) imaging successfully detected differences in photoacoustic signal intensity (PSI), blood oxygen saturation (SaO2), hemoglobin content (HbT), and heart volume in mouse embryos exposed to methylmercury chloride (MMC), which were consistent with findings from traditional histological methods.
